tasks.title: BUG-002: tokenizer overlap — defer to the containing base token for trailing-'_' literals
tasks.description: segment.ts pass 4's literal loop only defers on exact equal spans; a base token that strictly CONTAINS the trimmed literal span (trailing-'_' trim, e.g. tokenize('FOO_1_') → overlapping ['FOO_1'[0,5), 'FOO_1_'[0,6)]) is emitted alongside the literal, producing duplicate menu candidates. Fix: containment defer (o.start <= start && end <= o.end) + spec/04 'Strictly additive' bullet extension.

subtasks.title: Containment defer in tokenize pass 4 + segment tests + spec/04 sync
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: plan/004_24ebf0115d16/bugfix/001_1a2f4ffe408f/architecture/r2-tokenizer-overlap.md (all claims live-verified). '_' is the ONLY character in both BASE_RE's word class (segment.ts:75) and LITERAL_SYMBOL_CHARS (:109), so the trailing-'_' trim is the only straddle possible. The equal-span defer sits at segment.ts:569; the overlap-safety branch (:658-662) emits the literal AND keeps the straddling base (its '\b boundaries make this unreachable' comment is false for rule 4c — LITERAL_RE has no \b). Chosen fix (b) defer-to-containing-base: consistent with the equal-span defer and spec/04:104-105 ('literals absorb only strictly-contained tokens'); fix (a) overlap-absorption was REJECTED because it contradicts that spec clause and would complete 'FOO_1' by deleting a typed '_'.
2. INPUT: tokenize()'s pass-4 literal loop in src/core/segment.ts (~560-680): the out-cursor token o (first not-yet-passed token ending after start), the trimmed literal span [start, end), and the final merge's overlap-safety branch.
3. LOGIC: At segment.ts:569 change the defer condition from (o.start === start && o.end === end) to (o.start <= start && end <= o.end) — equality is the subset case; a kept base/hexish token that CONTAINS the trimmed literal span wins and no literal is emitted ('FOO_1_' keeps its base token). Update the overlap-safety comment at :660 (branch stays as a defensive guard; note the 4c caveat). Tests (TDD): raws('FOO_1_') === ['FOO_1_'] in the rule-4c describe block (test/segment.test.ts ~615+); add trailing-'_' inputs ('FOO_1_', 'rename FOO_1_ ok', 'USER_2_TOKEN_') to the disjoint-spans invariant cases (test/segment.test.ts:293-305). Adjacent invariants must keep passing: '2560x1440@2' absorption (:617-631 — strictly-contained bases still absorb; the new defer only fires when the BASE is the container), opaque-literal equal-span class pins (:679-690), hexish/CJK/path cases.
4. OUTPUT: tokenize() honoring its documented disjoint-span invariant (segment.ts:316) — one token for the trailing-'_' class; consumed by P1.M2.T1.S2's end-to-end assertion.
5. DOCS: Mode A — extend spec/04-tokenization-and-scoring.md's 'Strictly additive' bullet (:101-106): a literal whose post-trim span equals or is contained in a kept base/hexish/compound token defers to that token; add the FOO_1_ example. Lands with the code (AGENTS.md binding policy).

tasks.title: BUG-003: release widget suppression by dismissed-buffer fingerprint, not numeric start
tasks.description: createVisibilityMachine's suppression release compares numeric fragment starts (widget.ts:628-637), so a dismissal at start 0 (Tab acceptance, Escape, Enter-submit of a message's first word) never releases for the NEXT message's first word — also start 0 in the cleared buffer — silently hiding its completion line. Fix: record the dismissed buffer fingerprint and stay suppressed only while the current buffer is a same-word continuation.

subtasks.title: Record dismissed-buffer fingerprint and release suppression on context change
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: plan/004_24ebf0115d16/bugfix/001_1a2f4ffe408f/architecture/r3-suppression-leak.md (leak reproduced live for all three start-0 dismissal sites: Tab acceptance widget.ts:921, Escape/boundary-Esc :1117-1120, Enter-submit :1113-1119; onDismissed records the numeric start :707-721; the machine already computes lines.join('\n') per tick :598). Chosen fix: buffer-fingerprint release — the start===0+fresh-buffer heuristic was REJECTED (fragile, patches one symptom) and reset-on-submit was second choice (a new seam through editor.ts that misses hidden-Enter submits after a Tab acceptance).
2. INPUT: The evaluate R4 block as it stands AFTER P1.M1.T2.S1 — this subtask deliberately lands after the chain branch (both rewrite the same evaluate block; re-run BOTH test/widget.test.ts and test/widget-visibility.test.ts when done) — plus the per-tick buffer fingerprint.
3. LOGIC: In src/pi/widget.ts createVisibilityMachine: (a) add `let suppressedFingerprint: string | null = null` beside suppressedFragmentStart (:482); (b) in onDismissed(explicit) record lines.join('\n') as the fingerprint; if the dismissed buffer is EMPTY, keep suppressed=true but set the fingerprint to null meaning context-free — release at any boundary; (c) in the R4 release check (:628-637) stay suppressed only when (start === suppressedFragmentStart && sameWordContinuation), where sameWordContinuation = (fp !== null && (current.startsWith(fp) || fp.startsWith(current))) for the current fingerprint. Rationale: within one message, editing/extending/backspacing the dismissed word keeps one buffer a prefix of the other; a submitted-and-cleared buffer is neither, so the next message's first word (start 0) releases — spec/07:72-75 'Re-open only at the next word start or trigger char' intent restored. paint() clears both fields (:529-541); the trigger-char bypass (:628) stays untouched. Tests: fresh-buffer first word paints after each start-0 dismissal variant (Tab-accept, Escape, Enter-submit — mirror the PRD repro 'ze'→Tab→Enter then 'lw' must be visible); same-word backspace/edit STAYS suppressed; existing suppression pins (test/widget-visibility.test.ts:282/316/342; test/widget.test.ts suppression cases) keep passing — no must-change tests. UI-layer change: live TTY verification per spec/09. Assert composition with BUG-001: a zero-char chain offer at start 0 is exactly a released word start.
4. OUTPUT: Suppression scoped to the dismissed message's word; closes BUG-003.
5. DOCS: none — no spec wording change (restores existing spec/07:72-75 intent); no user-facing/config surface change beyond the fix.

tasks.title: BUG-004: carry partial tokens across 64KB slice boundaries in processText
tasks.description: IngestPipeline.processText tokenizes each ≤64KB slice independently, shredding a token that straddles a slice edge (junk trailing half admitted, real token lost, successor bigrams broken). Fix: carry each non-final slice's trailing token-class run into the next slice, mirroring the existing openLine/openTail run stitching, plus the spec/05 never-splits-a-token clause.

subtasks.title: Token carry in processText + docstring + spec/05 sync
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: plan/004_24ebf0115d16/bugfix/001_1a2f4ffe408f/architecture/r4-chunk-stitching.md (all claims live-verified: chunk loop ingest.ts:392-403 with #chunkBytes default 65_536 at :307; #admitSegment tokenizes slice-locally :465; the run layer DOES stitch across boundaries via appendSegment's openTail :190 — token stitching was intended but missing; the docstring :388-391 admits the 'accepted approximation'). Key traps from research: carried chars must NOT enter openTail accounting (trim BEFORE appendSegment sees the slice) or the 'zorpwibble quuxblat' run breaks; the per-iteration await this.#yieldFn() must fire even for an emptied slice (test/ingest-pipeline.test.ts:197 pins yield counts); the carry must be capped (a >64KB identifier would grow it unbounded).
2. INPUT: processText's slice loop (off += this.#chunkBytes) and its split('\n')/appendSegment/#admitSegment machinery; the five tokenize regexes' char classes (src/core/segment.ts:75-101) whose exact union is the token-continuation class.
3. LOGIC: In src/pi/ingest.ts add module consts near WHITESPACE_GAP_RE (~:154): `const TOKEN_CHAR_RE = /[A-Za-z0-9._@:+/~=-]/` (comment: keep in sync with the segment.ts regexes) and `const MAX_CARRY = 1024`. Restructure the loop with `let carry = ''`: per iteration prepend the PREVIOUS carry to the raw slice, then for NON-final slices trim the raw part's trailing TOKEN_CHAR run (capped at MAX_CARRY) into the next carry and feed the trimmed slice to the existing machinery unchanged — carried chars never enter slice N's admission (no double count) and openTail is computed from the trimmed slice. Final slice: carry nothing — text ending mid-token admits that token whole (restores single-slice semantics; the regexes need no right anchor). Replace the stale docstring at :388-391 with the carry contract. Mocking: none — real IngestPipeline over a real store; tests use the chunkBytes option for small-chunk analogues.
4. OUTPUT: No token split by a slice boundary; runs and bigrams form across boundaries; consumed by P1.M2.T3.S2's regression battery.
5. DOCS: Mode A — spec/05-ingestion-pipeline.md 'Chunked processing' (:30-36) gains: 'A slice boundary never splits a token: the trailing partial token (suffix of token-class characters) is carried into the next slice and tokenized there exactly once, mirroring the open-line/open-tail run carry.' Lands with the code.
